text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mixed in quiet dealings. By the close March stood at $304.60 per tonne, a gain of $0.50, while May ended flat at $301.80 per tonne. In New York raw sugar futures closed lower amid a lack of follow- through buying from the funds, which had carried the market to nearly three-week highs Thursday. However, fundamentals remain bearish so that there is no reason for a major rally. March lost 6 points to close at 10.60 cents/lb, while May gave up 3 points to close at 10.56 cents/lb.

MAURITIUS - Sugar production in 1996/97 amounted to 646,173 tonnes, raw value, up from 571,515 tonnes in 1995/96 and 529,671 tonnes in 1994/95. Sugar consumption in November 1996 reached 3,639 tonnes which brought cumulative consumption in the first six months of 1996/97 (June/November) up to 21,474 tonnes compared to 20,553 tonnes. In order to successfully conclude its export programme, Mauritius still has to import some sugar.
Sugar imports in November reached 3,194 tonnes, which brought cumulative imports in June/November 1996/97 up to 11,682 tonnes compared to nil in the like period in the previous year.
Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 38,086 tonnes.

Sugar exports in November 1996 amounted to 39,413 tonnes compared to 38,987 tonnes in November 1995. This brought cumulative exports in June/November 1996 up to 412,895 tonnes compared to 333,787 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 565,608 tonnes against 525,697 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in June/November 1996 were the UK with 290,184 tonnes raws against 299,391 tonnes, Portugal with 83,104 tonnes, up from 19,080 tonnes and the USA with 23,866 tonnes compared to 1,830 tonnes.

CANADA - Sugar imports in November 1996 amounted to 122,019 tonnes, raw value, up from 73,897 tonnes in November 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first two months of 1996/97 (October/November) up to 224,042 tonnes compared to 243,861 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 1.160 million tonnes compared to 1.013 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 1.212 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of origin in October/November 1996 were Australia with 198,947 tonnes raws against 224,776 tonnes and Brazil with 19,435 tonnes compared to nil. Brazil also was the largest white sugar supplier delivering 2,043 tonnes compared to nil.

SWITZERLAND - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 11,595 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 11,288 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October/December) up to 31,897 tonnes compared to 41,878 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 169,593 tonnes compared to 155,620 tonnes in 1994/95.
Major countries of origin in October/December 1996 were Germany with 22,315 tonnes compared to 28,059 tonnes and France with 5,945 tonnes, down from 9,480 tonnes.
